1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising __a hardware source and__ one or more logic circuits [[configured to at least:receive]] __that receive__ a plurality of independent first entropy values from [[a]] the hardware source; [[apply]] __apply__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; [[seed]] __seed__ a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; [[generate]] __generate__ a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded [[receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded]] with the second entropy value; and [[produce]] __produce__ a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number. [[produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.]]

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to produce]] __produce__ the block of ciphertext or message authentication code [[includes being configured to produce]] __by producing__ the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to produce]] __produce__ the block of ciphertext or message authentication code [[includes being configured to at least:implement]] __by at least implementing__ a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and [[produce]] __producing__ the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key. [[implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.]]

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to receive]] __receive__ the plurality of independent first entropy values [[includes being configured to receive]] __by receiving__ the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to receive]] __receive__ the plurality of independent first entropy values [[includes being configured to receive]] __by receiving__ the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the [[hardware source is a plurality of independent hardware sources]] __system comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources__, and the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to receive]] __receive__ the plurality of independent first entropy values [[includes being configured to receive]] __by receiving__ the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to apply]] __apply__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function [[includes being configured to apply]] __by applying__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to apply]] __apply__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function [[includes being configured to apply]] __by applying__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to apply]] __apply__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function [[includes being configured to apply]] __by applying__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to apply]] __apply__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function [[includes being configured to selectively apply]] __by selectively applying__ multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

(Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits [[being configured to apply]] __apply__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function [[includes being configured to apply]] __by applying__ at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

15. 17. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the [[hardware source is a plurality of independent hardware sources]] __method comprises receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from a plurality of independent hardware sources__.

22. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

24. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
